TWO backend security spec violations found: GET /api/companies/{cid}/navigation returns 200 with modules=[] instead of 404 for a non-existent company_id, and 200 with modules=[] instead of 403 when the caller has no membership on a company in the SAME workspace (verified: reporting user with only Meelora access got 200 on the CB navigation URL). No data leakage (modules=[], admin_view=false, no capabilities), but this is a spec violation per the review request ('la société sans accès=403, société inexistante=404'). Rated HIGH (spec) rather than BLOCKER because no financial/module data is disclosed and hidden legacy routes still correctly return 403.

minor.issue: Returns 200 with {workspace_id, company_id, admin_view:false, modules:[]} for a non-existent company_id instead of 404. No data leak but violates spec (société inexistante=404).

For a caller who has NO membership on the target company but is in the same workspace (e.g., persona_reporting on the CB/9434 company), the endpoint returns 200 with modules=[] instead of 403 (spec: 'société sans accès=403'). No modules or capabilities are leaked, but the endpoint should refuse.

action_items: Harden GET /api/companies/{company_id}/navigation to (1) return 404 when the company_id does not exist in the caller's workspace, and (2) return 403 when the caller has no company_membership/company_access/is_workspace_admin on that company. Currently build_company_navigation blindly loops NAV_MODULES with modules=[] as the practical outcome. Add an explicit access gate before the loop (mirror /api/companies/{cid}/members which already returns 403). Impact: closes spec item — 'company sans accès=403, société inexistante=404'.

rca of the issue: get_company_navigation (server.py:2455) delegates to access_nav.build_company_navigation without a prior existence/access check. build_company_navigation (core/access/navigation.py:82) iterates NAV_MODULES and only skips modules where authorize_module denies — the outer envelope {workspace_id, company_id, admin_view, modules} is always returned. For a non-existent company_id the iteration terminates trivially with modules=[]; for a company the caller cannot access, is_company_admin=false and every authorize_module call returns allowed=false, again producing modules=[]. Fix: guard at the route level with an explicit membership+existence check before delegating.
